verdict.rationale: Cloudflare documents strong prototype-to-scale continuity: Workers/D1/KV/Durable Objects use the same bindings and APIs at any traffic level, Agents SDK explicitly claims 'deploy once and Cloudflare runs your agents across its global network, scaling to tens of millions of instances,' and billing is compute-based rather than wall-time even for hibernating workloads (cloudflare-docs-15, cloudflare-supp-agents-sdk, cloudflare-docs-9). However, independent developer reports concretely contradict this for a real workload class: CPU-time limits (30s free / 15min paid) mean long-running AI agent tasks 'don't work,' forcing some teams toward self-hosting rather than staying on the same primitives (cloudflare-comm-9), and separate community feedback cites D1/KV vendor lock-in complicating running the same code elsewhere as it scales (cloudflare-comm-10). Missing for 10: benchmark/case-study evidence of a single app scaling from prototype to massive production traffic on identical Workers primitives without hitting CPU/duration ceilings, and resolution of the lock-in/portability concern.
